calls.video_title: What I'm Buying In The Most Disconnected Market I've Seen
calls.thesis: Reiterated BUY (last BUY 24 Nov). Buying aggressively. Meta's AI capex is paying off inside its own business: advertisers are seeing a 33% decline in cost per acquisition, Meta is adding the most advertising revenue per quarter versus Amazon and Google, and trailing-12-month revenue is $242B, growing 26%+ for three straight quarters.
calls.base: AI keeps improving ad targeting and revenue keeps compounding at 25%+.
calls.bull: Ad-share gains accelerate and Meta overtakes Google as the largest digital advertiser.
calls.bear: Capex keeps rising faster than the ad payoff, or advertiser demand softens.

calls.thesis: Added a lot on Friday; under $600, TTM P/E ~19, forward P/E under 18, revenue still growing 25%+ YoY; growing conviction on Muse, Meta's AI agent, from daily personal use (fixed his AdSense tax-treaty mix-up, recovering $7,000 from Google); Meta winning the most new ad dollars vs Google and Amazon.

Stance flips HOLD to BUY: in closing the Google earnings video he says his focus is still going to be on buying more Meta (and Amazon) in his portfolio rather than adding Google, because he believes those businesses offer a lot more value — Meta's advertising business is winning (added $13bn of ad revenue in Q3 vs Google's $7.8bn, growing 25%+ while Google's core decelerates) and is on track to overtake Google as the largest digital advertiser. Stated as a portfolio preference inside the Google video, not a standalone Meta recommendation; no price target given.

Messy Q3 but underlying profitability still growing: revenue up 26% YoY to $64.6B, a $9.89B legal charge suppressed operating income, free cash flow was negative this quarter (capex $34.91B vs operating cash flow $32.8B) and he expects negative FCF and some dilution from the new Class C share into 2027 — but he still thinks Meta is undervalued (updated DCF: 15% operating-cash-flow growth at 14x price/OCF gives ~17% annual compounding; ~23x normalised earnings if net margin returns to ~30%), so he continues holding and would increase the position if the shares come down more.
calls.price_at_call: Up ~5% in after-hours at recording; no share price stated (he was building his position when it was under $600 a couple of months ago)

calls.thesis: New BUY stance: extremely bullish on Meta — now #3 in AI models behind only Anthropic (ahead of OpenAI and Google) after the market wrote it off a few quarters ago; with its infrastructure it should sell tokens at great value.

calls.price: fair value $827 conservative / ~$1,000 realistic; ~$720s at video time
calls.thesis: Still undervalued despite +30% rally; Muse adoption (3M+ US downloads, #1 app) + free distribution across Instagram/WhatsApp; ad-ROI upside from user data; forward P/E ~23x for 20%+ grower.
calls.base: 20% annual OCF growth, 15x price/OCF = $1,000 FV, 22.6% CAGR over 3 years
calls.bull: Leading frontier model (watermelon) + hardware + agents revenue diversification
calls.bear: Savings-shared revenue monetization model unclear; Muse may disrupt, not yet monetize
calls.video_title: Why I Plan To Continue Buying Meta Stock

calls.thesis: Killer-app story is real but the easy money is made: 8.7x sales / 29x earnings is ~30% above the 5-yr average. Long-term investors will be rewarded, but wait for a pullback from the hype before buying big.
